Summary Collaboration Themes: This collaboration bridges applied nonlinear dynamics and pure arithmetic geometry by treating arithmetic invariants as dynamical variables. Jiang’s data-driven sparse identification (SINDy) and spectral analysis (Koopman/HAVOK) will be applied to discrete arithmetic data from LMFDB to discover minimal polynomial models of Hilbert Modular Surfaces and classify automorphic forms. Conversely, Martin’s number-theoretic constraints (Real Multiplication, Mestre Obstructions) will inform the structure of nonlinear dynamical models in power systems, providing rigorous bounds for stability analysis. The core innovation lies in using compressed sensing and sparse regression to recover high-dimensional algebraic structures from sparse data, and applying geometric minimization techniques to enhance the interpretability of data-driven dynamical models.
